item.title: A real taste of home!
item.description: Make sure you serve real South African samosas this Christmas or New Year.

item.title: Oh, what a night!
item.description: The recent USA4RSA gala event had all the ingredients of an unforgettable evening with stunningly dressed esteemed guests, the sounds of a top-notch Jazz band, rhythmic swing dancers on the dance floor and open hearts to contribute to a worthy cause.

item.title: Dragon boat race fun!
item.description: It has become a tradition for Friends of South Africa (FoSA) Nashville to compete in the city's annual Cumberland River Dragon boat races. This year FoSA entered two boats, The Vuvuzela Sharks and the Vuvuzela Sparks, with a total of 40 paddlers and two drummers dressed in our best zebra attire.

item.title: No one wears the pants in the McLean-Bailey household
item.description: When an internationally recognised television personality, emcee, speaker, entrepreneur and philanthropist, and a former Manchester United legend and England goalkeeper, soccer commentator, presenter and global circuit speaker team up, one can only expect fireworks!

item.title: Macadamia dream started on a Lowveld farm
item.description: Brandon Hiemstra grew up in Mbombela, Mpumalanga, an area abundant with fruits, nuts and vegetables. The city is surrounded with rich agricultural activities and in the past ten years the Lowveld has become one of South Africa’s major hubs for macadamia farming.

item.title: Innovation fits young entrepreneur like a glove
item.description: While Brandon Hiemstra turned to America to find new markets for SA-grown macadamias, a woman who grew up in rural South Africa is establishing herself in the business world, thanks in part to a USA programme that empowers female entrepreneurs.

item.title: South Africans in the USA reconnect over flames and friendship at SA Love's first Family Picnic
item.description: There’s something unmistakably comforting about the smell of a braai, the laughter of familiar accents, and the rhythm of a community gathering under open skies.

item.title: From homes to healing: Wanda Voight helps South Africans navigate life in the US
item.description: Immigration is rarely just about visas, jobs or new houses; it’s also about identity, belonging and resilience.

item.title: From love to legacy: How Wanda Voight builds homes, sisterhood and a call for justice
item.description: When South African-born psychotherapist turned entrepreneur Wanda Voight followed her heart to America, she thought her greatest challenges would be starting over and building a business in a new country. Instead, her path unfolded into something far greater.

item.title: Keeping the kettles boiling: How ‘Tannies Tee’ became a home away from home for South Africans in Nashville
item.description: When a cup of rooibos becomes more than just tea. Meet Kobie Pretorius, the woman behind Nashville’s beloved “Tannies Tee” — a monthly gathering turning strangers into family and homesickness into hope. From tennis courts to teapots, she’s building community one warm sip at a time.
